cells.tense: The pen is in your hand and you are drawing the lines that hold.
cells.act: ask how it feels to them and stay with the answer
cells.ask: When someone brings you something heavy, ask what it feels like on their side, and stay past your first fixing move.
cells.core:
Chaos arrives and the urge to make a container arrives with it. You don't reach first. A shape drawn from the ground up can carry a real load and leave the people inside it uncrushed. There's nothing here to correct. You can hold the plan open longer than the plan wants.
So ask. Ask what it feels like on their side, and stay with the answer a beat past where you'd normally start building. Nothing gets built in that beat, and nothing needs to be. The whole frame rests on the asking, and a frame that waits for the bearing line is stronger for the wait. The next line goes in once the person is done.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold weight while the person is still talking.

cells.tense: You are already sketching the frame of a thing that hasn't happened.
cells.act: weigh what it costs them against what it gives
cells.ask: Before the next plan lands, write two lines on paper: what it costs them and what it gives them. Build nothing from it yet.
cells.core:
When the outcome is still ahead, the structure gets drawn early — a frame for a feeling not yet here, a plan for a result nobody can see. It looks like building. It's a wall raised over ground that hasn't settled, and the person it's for hasn't been asked.
So weigh it. Before the next plan goes down, write two lines: what this costs them and what it gives them. On paper, not in your head. The point isn't a verdict, only a look at both columns at once. The figures on the page are usually not the ones you were carrying. The frame can stay open one page longer.
cells.sheetLine: You frame it before it's happened, and the frame keeps the person out.

cells.tense: The structure you built is standing and you are standing outside its door.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Choose one load you're still carrying that's already finished, and put it down within the day. Keep the unfinished ones.
cells.core:
You know how to build. The building is yours, and you're not inside it. Plans get made for other people and held by you; the structure stays level and whoever keeps it level is somewhere behind the present. Nothing can be pushed into that gap — pushing doesn't fit through it. Stepping back in isn't done by effort.
So put down something finished. Not the whole load, just a piece that's already done, out of your hands today. Keep the unfinished ones; they're supposed to be there. A door opens on the far side of a single thing you've stopped carrying.
cells.sheetLine: You built the frame and stopped standing inside it.

cells.tense: The structure is holding and your name is not on any part of it.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin one thing this week with no plan past its first day. Let the starting belong to you.
cells.core:
The plan is steady, the moves land, the thing holds — and the account of it reads as if nobody drew it. The builder has stepped outside the frame and hasn't stepped back in. The pressure isn't on the structure; the structure is fine. It's on the record that stopped coming back around, and the record is the part left to bring in.
So begin something with no plan past the first day. A spark, a first sketch, a thing that hasn't decided what it's for. Beginning it is the whole point. There's no wall to raise yet and no one to hold it for — just the start, which is already yours. Stand in it; the frame will follow.
cells.sheetLine: The frame is yours and the reckoning has gone missing.
